concepts.name: Pinyin initials and finals
concepts.summary: Read and pronounce pinyin syllables by combining initials and finals, including distinctive sounds such as zh/ch/sh, q, x, ü.

concepts.name: Four tones and neutral tone
concepts.summary: Distinguish and produce the high-level, rising, dipping and falling tones plus the unstressed neutral tone, and recognise that tone changes word meaning.

concepts.name: Stroke order rules
concepts.summary: Write simple characters using the standard rules such as top to bottom, left to right, and horizontal before vertical.

concepts.name: Radicals as character components
concepts.summary: Recognise common radicals like 氵, 亻, 口 and 木 and know they often hint at meaning.

concepts.name: Basic SVO word order
concepts.summary: Build simple statements with subject-verb-object order and no verb conjugation, e.g. 我喝茶.

concepts.name: Core greetings and numbers
concepts.summary: Recall greetings, pronouns, numbers 1–99 and the first set of HSK 1 words in simplified characters.

concepts.name: Yes-no questions with ma and ne
concepts.summary: Form basic questions by adding 吗 to statements or 呢 for follow-up questions.

misconceptions.text: Tones are optional extras that native speakers will ignore if the word is clear from context.
Pinyin letters are pronounced like the same English letters, so q is like English q and x like English x.
The order in which you draw strokes does not matter as long as the finished character looks right.

concepts.name: Tone sandhi for third tone
concepts.summary: Apply the rule that a third tone before another third tone is pronounced as second tone, as well as 不 and 一 tone changes.

concepts.name: Measure words with numbers
concepts.summary: Use common measure words like 个, 本, 杯 and 张 between a number or demonstrative and a noun.

concepts.name: Completed action le
concepts.summary: Use 了 after a verb to mark completed actions and distinguish it from sentence-final 了 marking change of state.

concepts.name: Experiential guo
concepts.summary: Use 过 after a verb to say one has had an experience, and negate it with 没.

concepts.name: Time words and word position
concepts.summary: Place time and location phrases before the verb and order them correctly in a sentence.

concepts.name: Negation with bu and mei
concepts.summary: Choose 不 for habitual, future or stative negation and 没(有) for past events and possession.

concepts.name: Radical-based character lookup
concepts.summary: Use radicals and phonetic components to guess meaning or sound and find characters in a dictionary, across HSK 1–2 vocabulary.

concepts.name: Question words in place
concepts.summary: Form questions with 什么, 谁, 哪, 几 and 怎么 in the position of the answer, without fronting.

misconceptions.text: The particle 了 is the past tense marker and goes on every past-time sentence.
Measure words can be dropped, so 三书 is as correct as 三本书.
不 and 没 are interchangeable ways of saying 'not'.

concepts.name: Durative zhe
concepts.summary: Use 着 to express ongoing states or manner, and contrast it with 在 for progressive actions.

concepts.name: Resultative and directional complements
concepts.summary: Attach complements such as 完, 到, 好, 上来 to verbs to express result or direction.

concepts.name: Ba construction structure
concepts.summary: Build 把 sentences with subject + 把 + definite object + verb + complement, showing what is done to the object.

concepts.name: Bei passive construction
concepts.summary: Form passives with 被 (and 叫/让) plus an agent and a verb with a complement, often with adverse or notable results.

concepts.name: Aspect particle contrast
concepts.summary: Analyse a context to choose between 了, 过, 着 and 在, explaining the difference in meaning.

concepts.name: Degree and potential complements
concepts.summary: Use 得 to describe manner or degree and 得/不 potential forms like 听得懂 and 看不见.

concepts.name: HSK 3–4 vocabulary by word formation
concepts.summary: Learn HSK 3–4 vocabulary by analysing how compounds are built from known characters and morphemes.

misconceptions.text: The 把 construction can be used with any verb and any object.
The 被 passive is used wherever English uses a passive, so it is neutral and very common.
着 is just the Chinese equivalent of the English -ing ending.

concepts.name: Sentence-final le versus verb le
concepts.summary: Analyse sentences with both verbal and sentence-final 了 and explain how they differ in meaning and implication.

concepts.name: Ba and bei semantic constraints
concepts.summary: Judge when 把 or 被 is required, optional or unacceptable based on definiteness, affectedness and complement type.

concepts.name: Topic-comment structure
concepts.summary: Analyse how topics are fronted and how subjects can be omitted when recoverable from context.

concepts.name: Conjunctions and connective pairs
concepts.summary: Use paired connectors such as 虽然…但是, 不但…而且 and 即使…也 to structure complex arguments.

concepts.name: Register and spoken versus written
concepts.summary: Evaluate word choice between colloquial and formal equivalents such as 吃 and 食用 or 因此 and 所以.

concepts.name: HSK 5–6 vocabulary and chengyu
concepts.summary: Interpret and use common four-character idioms and HSK 5–6 vocabulary in context.

concepts.name: Reading unseen characters
concepts.summary: Infer meaning and approximate sound of unfamiliar characters from phonetic and semantic components, knowing the limits of such inference.

misconceptions.text: Sentence-final 了 and verb 了 are the same particle with the same meaning in any position.
Every sentence must have an explicit subject, and dropping it is sloppy.
A character's phonetic component always gives its exact pronunciation and tone.

concepts.name: Evaluating aspect usage in discourse
aliases: discourse use of le guo zhe
concepts.summary: Evaluate native and learner texts for how aspect particles organise narrative sequence, background and foregrounding.

concepts.name: Prosody and intonation across tones
concepts.summary: Judge how tones interact with stress, rhythm and sentence intonation in connected speech and correct nonnative patterns.

concepts.name: Stylistic composition across registers
concepts.summary: Compose texts such as emails, essays and speeches in suitable registers using appropriate syntax and idiom.

concepts.name: Regional variation and Mandarin norms
concepts.summary: Evaluate differences between putonghua, regional accents and Taiwan Mandarin in vocabulary, pronunciation and script.

concepts.name: Classical Chinese in modern usage
concepts.summary: Assess how classical grammar and vocabulary persist in idioms, formal writing and set phrases.

concepts.name: Designing teaching and study materials
concepts.summary: Create graded materials and explanations that sequence grammar, characters and vocabulary for specific learner groups.

concepts.name: Translation and nuance equivalence
concepts.summary: Produce translations that preserve nuance, deciding on how to render aspect, measure words and omitted subjects.

misconceptions.text: Mandarin has no grammar to speak of, so fluency is mostly a matter of memorising vocabulary.
Taiwan and mainland Mandarin differ only in script, not in vocabulary or pronunciation.
Faithful translation means matching each Chinese particle with an English tense or word.
